# <span id="aanchor485"></span> Batch Schedule Editor

Accessing this form requires **System Process – System Information** privileges and the **Liquids** add-on.

Batch schedules can be assigned to a liquid meter to automatically create batches for meters that deliver batches on a known schedule, with known products. You can assign a different batch schedule for a meter on a month-by-month basis if the product flow changes, or if the day of the month that the batch starts on changes.

The use of a batch schedule can be helpful if batches are hand-keyed into the system, or if the import file does not contain the batch start/stop or the batch product information.

When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in meter characteristics on the day specified in the schedule.

The Batch Schedule Editor is used to create monthly schedules. To create an annual schedule, use the [Annual Schedule Editor](../Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md).

<div class="procedure">

To create a monthly batch schedule:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.

2.  Select **Batch Schedule Editor** within the **Liquids** group.

3.  Click the **New** button.

4.  Enter a schedule name and description.

5.  Double-click each day to include in the schedule. As days are selected, they will display in the grid to the right.

    Selected days will display with a yellow highlight. To de-select a day, double-click it again.

6.  Click the down arrow for each day to define a product.

7.  Click the **Save** button.

Once created, the batch schedule can be assigned to a liquid meter in the Meter Editor (Liquids tab \> Schedules sub-tab).



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 531;height: 333;" />

</div>

For FLOWCAL to create batches based on a batch schedule, the Batch Scheduler utility (FcBatchScheduler.exe) must be run. If the the Batch Scheduler utility is run, but cannot create batches on a meter because it is locked by another process, such as meter rollups or a user performing edits, no messages will be generated. The utility should be run during off hours to minimize the chances of this happening and to minimize database access during peak hours. For additional details, see: [Batch Scheduler Utility](Batch%20Scheduler%20Utility.md).
